proposal.title: Kajenn Press: the site tab, page Bags and per-page publication
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: The administration mirrors the data model and the API instead of the operator's tasks. The navigation groups are record kinds and the buttons are service operations. An operator who wants a site online meets templates in Python, channels, routes, candidates, builds and generations before seeing a result.
This proposal designs the administration from the operator's point of view first. The inventory of code changes comes after the design is agreed.

current.fact: The navigation tree of a site has one group per record kind: Pages, Templates, Styles, Scripts, Media.
The only creation entry in the tree is New page; Templates, Styles, Scripts and Media have none.
The New page workspace supports one HTML block named body and opens with a Gramlot template in Python to write or save first.
A build needs a channel first; the page shows "Save a channel first."
A page without a route cannot be selected for a build; the operator finds out only in Publishing.
Open tabs keep their original site when the site selector changes; the guide asks the operator to check the tab title.

list.item: The published image is static. Only the editor changes it.
Sites are always served by Kajenn under its rules. A fully static site is a choice, not a limit: a slot can be a dynamic iframe backed by Gramlot and the database.
Versioning is delegated to S3. Kajenn Press keeps no version history of its own.
Pages hold autonomous copies of templates, contents and assets. Every copy carries the id of its original, so all copies of an original can be found and updated on request.
A site can speak several languages; one is the main language (see Languages).

section.title: Navigation
section.code: Sites kajenn.org genro.com acme.org -new site- Library (shared CSS, common Gramlot templates, ...)

list.item: Selecting a site opens its site tab. Each site has its own tab.
-new site- opens an empty site tab. It can start empty or from a starting site: a source zip kept in Library.
Library holds what several sites share: CSS, common Gramlot templates, media.

section.title: The site tab
section.p: The site tab has three tabs: Visual editor, SEO, Published site.

section.title: Visual editor

list.item: The center shows the site rendered as it would be served locally. It opens on the root page; the operator moves to other pages through the links, as a visitor would.
On command, a very thin border marks every slot.
A block can be detached into a floating window with three tabs: CodeMirror (source), Jodit (visual editing), Preview.

section.p: A side drawer holds a tab container with two tabs.

list.item: Pages: a logical tree of all pages, managed with drag and drop. The tree organises the editing only; public URLs are independent of it. Every page expands into the named slots of its template. A page that no link reaches is still reachable here.
Contents: the contents of the site. A content used nowhere is shown in italic grey; used once, normal; used more than once, normal with a badge giving the number of uses.

section.p: A content is dragged into an empty slot, either on the slot in the rendered page or on the slot node in the Pages tree.
Every page and template in the tree shows two marks: changed since the last publication, and holding copies that are older than their original.

list.item: Every page has its own SEO: title, description, public URL, canonical, robots, Open Graph and social card, JSON-LD, image alt texts.

The root page has the most complete SEO and holds the site defaults: site name, sharing image, organisation, robots. An empty field of a page takes the root value; the tab shows that value beside the empty field.
The tab shows how the page looks in a search result and in a social share.
Before publishing it reports missing or duplicate titles, missing descriptions, images without alt and broken internal links.
Changing the URL of a page creates a 301 redirect from the old URL.
The 404 page of the site is an ordinary page.
The renderer reads all SEO data from here; sitemap.xml and robots.txt are generated at every publication.
A command top bar and, in the center, an iframe on the published site.
The top bar holds publication, rollback and the management commands, such as maintenance mode.
Maintenance mode makes Kajenn serve a maintenance page; the editor keeps seeing the real site through a private link.
An optional step publishes to a private address of the same server first, then makes it public.
The published site can have its own administration when needed. Its content is not designed here; Kajenn, Asqueel and Gramlot can build it.
A page is a Bag holding a template Bag (always a copy, however made), a contents Bag and the other assets. A page can produce its static HTML.
A template is a Bag of Gramlot source: nested containers. It declares its slots.

A slot is any object able to host content (a content pane, a div, a grid or table cell) that the author marks with kpress_slot. The value is True or a unique name. Every container has a node_label, set by the author or automatic, so every slot also has a path such as center.info.top.tab1.
Slot kinds: HTML, Markdown, dynamic iframe, content computed by a resolver. Empty slots are reported before publishing.

Templates live on three levels: Library (generic), site, page. A site template inherits from a Library template; the operator chooses linked (Library changes reach it) or independent copy. A linked template is the Library Bag plus the site's additions, removals and changes of nodes. A page-local customised copy is a later option.

section.title: Copies and updates

list.item: The operator edits a content, a template or an asset and sees the result.
Update shows the pages that hold a copy of it and the differences. Pages whose copy has local changes are flagged and start unselected.
The confirmed pages get the new copy and are rendered again. Update and publish can run as one step, so changing a shared CSS is one operation.

section.p: The badge in Contents counts the copies that carry the same original id.

row.cell: one zipped Bag with everything; the editor unpacks it, works and zips it again
one S3 version per deliberate save
the page Bag, possibly zipped: sources in one branch, pre-rendered pure HTML in a parallel branch
one S3 version per publication of the page

list.item: Rolling back a page restores the previous S3 version of its object. Rolling back the site restores a previous source zip and republishes the pages.
A complete site travels as one source zip: move, backup, handover, starting site.
Publish lists the pages changed since the last publication, all selected; the operator can unselect some and confirms.

A published page holds what is needed to render it again at any time. Its Python template can read the database or do other work at render time through resolvers, with a cache of, for example, 10 minutes.
Re-rendered HTML is stored on the local filesystem of the serving server, not on S3. S3 holds only what the editor published. A new publication of a page discards its local copy.

section.title: First publication
section.p: The Published site tab of a site never published guides the operator:

list.item: Choose the server among the ones registered in Kajenn Press.
Enter the domain and choose which of the domain and www. is the address; the other answers 301 to it.

DNS: Kajenn Press shows the exact records to create (A and AAAA for both names, towards the server's addresses) and checks when they become visible. Creating them through a provider's API comes later, Route 53 first.
Publish: the pages are published, the server's agent configures the proxy for the domain and obtains the certificate, and the tab shows the outcome.
The address is checked and the site appears in the Published site iframe.

section.p: A site can move to another server: the binding moves and the tab shows the new DNS records to create.
Whether a Python process is needed to re-render follows from the presence of resolvers in the templates; the operator is not asked.

list.item: A server is a host that runs the Kajenn site server image. Kajenn Press keeps a registry of servers: name, public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, the address of its agent. Every server reads the same release bucket; each site's binding names the server that serves it.
TLS comes from the proxy already installed on the server: nginx with certbot, Caddy or Traefik. Kajenn Press provides the site server image, which speaks plain HTTP, and one driver per proxy.

Each server runs an agent: a small Kajenn application that Kajenn Press calls to add or remove a domain, read the state of its certificate and reload the proxy. The agent has a fixed set of actions and no generic shell, answers only the manager with its own token on a limited network, and runs as a user without root, allowed by sudo only to reload the proxy and run certbot.
The manager host on Hetzner stays a manager: public sites are served by separate servers.

section.title: Help me
section.p: The site tab has a Help me button that opens a chat with Sonnet. Sonnet knows how Kajenn Press works, helps the user say what to create, offers fonts and colours, draws SVG elements such as logo and icons, and creates everything needed.

list.item: Choices appear as clickable previews: palettes, font pairs, logo versions.
Sonnet works through the MCP operations; the result is ordinary pages, templates and contents, editable by hand.
The visual editor shows the site taking shape beside the chat.
Help me is available on a new site and on an existing one.
The conversation is kept with the site and can be resumed.
Sonnet creates and saves; publishing stays an operator command.
One API key per Kajenn Press installation, part of the standard configuration.
Tokens and cost are shown per chat and in total per site, for information only: no budget, no limit while the tool is used internally.

section.title: Languages
section.p: A site has a main language and may have others. A page exists once; its texts exist once per language.

list.item: Each content has one version per language. The template is shared: its own texts, such as menu and footer, are page data and are translated like contents.
URLs carry the language as a prefix, such as /it/chi-siamo/ and /en/about/; the main language also answers without prefix.
A missing translation shows the text of the main language, and the editor marks it as missing.
When a text of the main language changes, its translations are marked as to update, as copies are today.
A language selector in the site bar sets the language of the Visual editor, the SEO tab and the preview. The Contents tree shows what is missing or to update in that language.
Title, description and URL are per language; the versions of a page point to each other with hreflang; the sitemap lists every language; the site defaults of the root page are per language.
Help me can propose translations; the operator confirms them, and proposed translations stay marked to review until then.
The published site offers a language selector in the template. The root never redirects by the browser's language.

section.title: Editing by several people
section.p: A site is edited by one person at a time. Whoever opens the editor takes the site; the others see who holds it and can only look. This prevents a second editor's zip from overwriting the first one's work.

decision.question: How does the operator choose and create a site?

option.title: Sites and Library in the navigation tree; one tab per site
Site selector in the top bar and New site dialog (today)

decision.choice: Everything about a site lives in its tab.

decision.question: Does a page hold references to contents or copies?

option.title: References
option.p: A change shows everywhere at once.

option.title: Autonomous copies carrying the original id
option.p: The operator edits, checks, then asks to update the copies.

decision.choice: Changes never propagate by accident.

decision.question: How is a slot identified?

option.title: Path of node labels
kpress_slot attribute declared by the template, True or a unique name

decision.choice: Every template declares its slots.

decision.question: Does a site template follow later changes of its Library template?

option.title: Linked
Independent copy
The operator chooses

decision.choice: A linked template is the Library Bag plus the site's node changes.

decision.question: What is published and how is it versioned?

option.title: One object per site
One object per page; source as one zip per site

decision.choice: S3 versions each page; the site travels as one zip.

decision.question: Where does re-rendered HTML go?

option.title: Written back to S3
option.p: Every re-render creates a new S3 version.

option.title: Local filesystem of the serving server

decision.choice: S3 holds only what the editor published.

decision.question: Where does an empty SEO field of a page take its value?

option.title: From the root page
From the page above in the tree
option.p: Moving a page in the tree would change its published SEO.

decision.choice: The tree is for editing only.

decision.question: Which pages does Publish publish?

option.title: Changed pages, all selected, the operator can unselect
All pages

decision.choice: One click in the usual case; a page not ready can stay back.

decision.question: Does Help me limit token consumption?

option.title: Information only
Budget with a limit

decision.choice: The tool is used internally for now.

decision.question: How do two people edit the same site?

option.title: One editor at a time per site
option.p: The lock expires after inactivity (for example 30 minutes); another user can take the site with an explicit command, warning the holder, whose unsaved changes are lost; Help me works under the lock of the user who opened it.

option.title: Concurrent editing with merge of the source zip
option.p: Needs a merge of the same Bag and conflict resolution per node; nothing provides it today.

decision.choice: The source is one zip; a merge mechanism does not exist.

decision.question: When a page changed its copy of a content, does Update overwrite it, skip it or ask?

option.title: Always overwrite
Always skip
Flag and let the operator choose
option.p: Pages with local changes are flagged and start unselected; selecting one shows the differences and overwrites on confirmation. Each copy carries the original id and the digest of the original at copy time; a different current digest means a local change.

decision.choice: Nothing is lost without the operator seeing it.

decision.question: When a Library template changes a node that a linked site template changed or removed, which version wins?

option.title: The site wins
The Library wins
Report and let the operator choose per node
option.p: The update of that template stops and lists the conflicting nodes, including renamed labels; per node the operator keeps the site version or takes the Library one. Until then the site template stays on the Library version it records.

decision.choice: Same rule as Update of copies.

decision.question: What do pages show when their template no longer declares a slot that held a content?

option.title: The copy is discarded
The copy stays without a slot
option.p: The page does not show it; the Pages tree lists it under the page as without slot, with a warning; the check before Publish reports it; the operator moves or deletes it.

option.title: The template cannot be saved while pages use the slot

decision.choice: Nothing is lost and templates stay free to change.

decision.question: When a page switches template, do slots with the same name keep their contents?

option.title: By name
All contents become without slot
Guided mapping
option.p: A panel shows old and new slots matched by name; the operator corrects and confirms; unmatched contents become without slot.

decision.choice: Equal names need one confirmation; renamed slots are seen before contents are detached.

decision.question: Content in dynamic iframes is not indexed. How does a page with dynamic slots stay indexable?

option.title: Accept: iframe content is not indexed
Dynamic iframes only on noindex pages
Static fallback content in the iframe slot
option.p: Written by hand or produced by a resolver, rendered in the page HTML and indexed; the iframe replaces it when the browser loads it. The SEO tab warns when an indexed page has an iframe slot without fallback.

decision.choice: Iframes stay free and pages do not reach search engines or no-JS readers empty.

decision.question: How does a resolver in the render worker reach a database?

option.title: Named connections in the server deployment
option.p: The Kajenn server's .env and secrets define named connections; the page Bag names the connection only; the worker receives it per render. Credentials never enter a Bag or S3.

option.title: Resolvers in the server process
Resolvers call HTTP APIs with a token

decision.choice: Credentials stay out of files that move and are versioned.

decision.question: Is resolver output filtered?

option.title: Text by default, HTML through nh3
Trusted like the template

decision.choice: Database values can hold text written by users.

decision.question: Do mutations keep idempotency keys?

option.title: Keep keys; receipts kept 24 hours in the site working copy
Drop keys; clients re-read before retrying

decision.choice: Help me makes many MCP calls and may retry them.

decision.question: Is there an audit of changes?

option.title: Minimal log in the site Bag
option.p: Who, when and what for each save, Publish, rollback and lock take; Help me actions are recorded as made by the user through Help me; the log travels with the zip.

option.title: No audit

decision.choice: An S3 version does not say who changed what.

decision.question: How do clicks and drops reach slots in the sandboxed preview?

option.title: A script in the preview with postMessage
option.p: sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-same-origin; the script is added to the preview HTML only, never to published HTML. Verified as the first step of N5; if native drag into the sandboxed iframe fails, the first version keeps click-to-select in the preview and drop on the Pages tree.

option.title: Page in the administration document inside a shadow DOM
Cross-window drag and drop in Gramlot

decision.choice: The administration stays isolated from the page.

decision.question: What happens to the Kajenn Press site in the Hetzner catalog?

option.title: Rebuild from the example sources
option.p: No migration code; the catalog volume is archived with the backup command of deploy/docker/HETZNER.md before the new version is installed.

option.title: Migrate with a converter

decision.choice: The site comes from examples/kajenn_press_site and its text must be rewritten anyway.

decision.question: What is translated?

option.title: The contents of one page, one version per language; one shared template
One page per language, linked to its translations

decision.choice: One page, one structure: layout changes reach every language.

decision.question: How do URLs carry the language?

option.title: A prefix per language; the main language also without prefix
One domain per language

decision.choice: One address per site, one binding.

decision.question: How are the template's own texts translated?

option.title: The template reads them from page data, translated like contents
One template per language

decision.choice: One template per site keeps one layout.

decision.question: What does a page show when a translation is missing?

option.title: The text of the main language, marked as missing in the editor
The page does not exist in that language

decision.choice: A visitor never meets a hole.

decision.question: What happens to translations when the main text changes?

option.title: They are marked as to update, as copies are
Nothing

decision.choice: The operator sees what is behind.

decision.question: How does the editor show languages?

option.title: A language selector in the site bar for the Visual editor, SEO and preview
Languages side by side

decision.choice: One language at a time keeps the tab as it is.

decision.question: How does SEO handle languages?

option.title: Title, description and URL per language, hreflang, every language in the sitemap
SEO in the main language only

decision.choice: Search engines index each language.

decision.question: Does Help me translate?

option.title: It proposes translations, marked to review until the operator confirms
No automatic translation

decision.choice: Drafts save time; the operator stays responsible.

decision.question: How does a visitor change language?

option.title: A selector in the template; no redirect by browser language
Automatic redirect from the root

decision.choice: Every URL shows the same page to everyone, robots included.

decision.question: Where does TLS come from?

option.title: The proxy installed on the server (nginx, Caddy, Traefik), through a driver per proxy
Caddy always, in front of every site server
An ACME client inside Kajenn

decision.choice: Kajenn Press provides the image; the host keeps its own proxy.

decision.question: How does Kajenn Press act on a server?

option.title: An agent application with fixed actions, called by the manager
A script on the server, run by a timer, reading the bindings

decision.choice: The tab shows the outcome at once; no generic shell, own token, limited network, no root.

decision.question: What is a server and where is it registered?

option.title: Registered in the source bucket; every server reads one release bucket; bindings name the server
One release bucket per server, in the installation's configuration

decision.choice: Adding a server needs no restart; moving a site moves one binding.

decision.question: How is DNS set up?

option.title: Show the records and check them; provider APIs later, Route 53 first
Route 53 credentials from the start

decision.choice: Works with any provider today.

decision.question: How are the domain and www served?

option.title: One is the address; the other answers 301 to it
Only the name entered

decision.choice: Visitors reach the site with or without www, on one canonical address.

decision.question: Does the Hetzner manager host serve public sites?

option.title: No: public sites go to separate servers
Yes, behind its nginx

decision.choice: The manager keeps the source keys away from public traffic.

consequences.p: This proposal replaces the navigation and the editors of : the site selector, the per-kind groups, the New page workspace and the publishing panel.

The publication model changes: channels, routes, candidates, builds and releases give way to per-page published objects versioned by S3 and a source zip per site. The catalog's own revision history is no longer the versioning mechanism.
A shared asset copied into every page costs storage per page, and changing it means updating and republishing every page that holds it.
The inventory of code changes is a separate step, after this design is agreed.
